Perfume rating 3.92 out of 5 with 6,780 votes

Megamare by Orto Parisi is a Aromatic Aquatic fragrance for women and men. Megamare was launched in 2019. The nose behind this fragrance is Alessandro Gualtieri. Top notes are Bergamot and Lemon; middle notes are Seaweed, Calone and Hedione; base notes are Musk, Ambroxan and Cedar.

"Alessandro Gualtieri's new olfactory creation is Megamare. With this fragrance the master perfumer exploits the richness and originality of the marine notes. Marine accords know how to arouse emotions with a soothing effect. In addition to that, the watery essences are capable of recalling pleasant associations, releasing romance and making us happy. Alessandro Gualtieri does not discover the secret of the olfactory bouquet of his fragrance." - a note from the brand.

AquaticJoe 12/08/25 13:10

Ah yes, Megamare. An "ultra-niche" staple not only among marine fragrances but within niche perfumery in general. Let’s take a closer look at what this one is all about.

When you first spray Megamare, whether on a tester strip or directly on skin, the very first thing you notice is just how strong it is. If you put this on your hand, you probably won’t need to bring it anywhere near your nose to catch a whiff. The opening does give you a touch of lemon, but it’s quickly mixed with a sharp calone and seaweed blend. As it begins to dry down, that almost piercing seaweed note really comes forward on its own, paired with ambroxan, while the musk settles into something that feels darker and slightly brooding.

After about three to four hours, it does calm down a bit, but that punchy seaweed stays front and center for the entire life of the fragrance. I personally enjoy Megamare, and I think what makes it so divisive is exactly this strength.

I’m preaching to the choir here, but regardless of how you feel about this scent profile, it’s probably best to go light on the sprays. With the mix of calone, ambroxan, and that sharp marine seaweed, this can easily become too much for people around you. Even with that in mind, this fragrance remains a beast and a true staple in the world of briny sea niche scents, and it has the famous performance to boot.

P.S.

If you like this general scent profile but feel Megamare is a little too intense, there are great options with similar vibes that go a bit easier on the senses while maintaining the similar unique briny DNA found here.

If you want something more designer-leaning that tones down the seaweed and boosts cleaner sea notes while keeping a darker marine feel, Black Sea by Lorenzo Pazzaglia is a great choice.

If you want something with a similarly sharp opening but slightly a more citrus, cypress, woody, and cleaner musk dry down, Blu Mare from Giardini di Toscana fits perfectly.

Both of these also perform extremely well, so you aren’t losing much in that department. Either way, diving into these scents is a rewarding adventure for anyone who loves bold, oceanic fragrances.

melomakarona 11/29/25 17:05

Megamare took me by surprise.

I am rarely seduced by marine scents, they often smell like straight seaweed and dirty waters. Yet this one is different. It evokes the sea in a very transportive way, and then wraps itself around me with a kind of clarity, maybe from the bright notes.

There is an unmistakable “fresh-from-the-waves” sensation here, very mineral, but purified, refined, like you had the time to dry-off and shake some cocktail after slicing lemons, where the zest splashed on your fingers. A very romanticized Mediterranean moment.

Marine scents can easily become overwhelming, even tyrannical, so I approached the spraying with caution and gave it only a single spray on the wrist. It gave me a steady, graceful presence from beginning to end.

Nothing struck me as jarring or excessive, a welcomed contrast to something like Aphtoblue where I rushed to wash it off.

Megamare is, simply put, beautiful: sunlit, saline, and Mediterranean to its very core. I am not sure how well someone could pull this off in a city without a sea close, but it is definitely wearable and appreciable if sprayed in moderation.









annalisaaffinito 11/20/25 13:49

Disclaimer: I'm not a Gualtieri fan. Not that I don't appreciate his creativity, but, save for two or three of his scents, I couldn't wear the rest because they bother me and make me feel dirty, which is the antithesis of my idea of a perfume and what I look for when I wear it. For this very reason, I've started to lose interest in Nasomatto, but even more so in Orto Parisi, of which, to be honest, I don't appreciate anything. And Megamare is no exception, but the immense debate surrounding it (I've read everything and the opposite of everything) made me curious to test it out thoroughly.

I finally understood the reason for this fragrance's great success. It's essentially the fusion of two trends that have dominated in recent years: the burnt "amber-musky" base notes, which have a distinctive scent common to perfumes like Baccarat Rouge, Annone, Turath, and Instant Crush, and the seaweedy marine scent typical of perfumes like Acqua di Sale, which has been smelt practically everywhere here in Rome. Put the two together and you get a multifaceted olfactory bomb, which at times is more of a smell than a perfume, which is both captivating and repulsive.

I agree with Melly (I nod along the way) and especially with the fragrance expert who let me try it in the boutique: Megamare is absolutely not an aquatic, ozonic perfume. It doesn't evoke the sea per se, but rather rather melancholic and decadent marine contexts. Above all, it's not a fresh, summery scent. Its scent reminds me of a wooden box I had as a child that came from a ship—a mix of stale wood that smells a bit like salt water, macerated seaweed, and a vague hint of kerosene. That smell, like Megamare, was both attractive and repulsive to me.

Who would I recommend Megamare to?
Well, first of all, to those who are fans of both macerated seaweed and burnt amber-musk. If either isn't your thing, leave it alone, it's not for you. I find it unisex, perhaps more masculine, and given the intensity of the fragrance, it needs to be dosed carefully, and I wouldn't use it in the height of summer, especially not in small, enclosed spaces.
I read in the comments that it was diluted, that it doesn't last long, etc., etc., um... can I tell you that's complete nonsense? Tried from an unopened, recently opened bottle, the perfume lingered on me for almost 24 hours and even left its scent on the pillow and sheets of the bed I slept in. In short, monstrous performance, absolutely out of the ordinary.

Again, I understand its success, but please be careful with the sprays: it easily becomes invasive and is the kind of perfume that can be quite nauseating for some people.

Merlynnthegreat 11/14/25 13:08

I definitely think this is a love it or hate it scent. It definitely gives off oceanic, but not in a stinky unpleasant way. Seaweed often smells fishy but here it's very well balanced with just enough to give ocean, but not overpower the other notes.

It reminds me of the the smell of a northern road, Rocky coastal beach, like in the Pacific Northwest. It's cold, it's wet, but it's definitely not unpleasant. The best way I feel I can describe it is like a waterlogged piece of driftwood on a rocky beach in cold weather. All of the notes blend really well together and are easily identifiable on their own, and each of them blends a depth and well roundedness to the scent.

As for the longevity, it absolutely lives up to its reputation.
It is 38 hours since I have initially applied the perfume and I still smell the Cedar notes well enough that I cannot put on something different and it has not washed off. I did not apply lotion or any moisturizer. Before applying the perfume, because I don't always moisturize before applying a perfume and I don't think that everybody is going to consider that when putting a scent like this on. It can and will transfer you to your clothing even if it is dry on your skin before you put your clothes on. A little goes a long way. I used two sprays on one arm transfer that to the other and one spray on my sternum. The arm that had the transfer lasted about 12 hours. The arm I sprayed on still carries the scent. Normally I wait to write a review until after the scent has completely disappeared from my skin. At this point I don't know if it's ever going to disappear fully.




Marck Menke 11/13/25 13:16

To again explore the comparison between Atlas and Megamare remains an exercise, both pointless and intriguing.
Pointless because obviously both scents are overwhelmingly dominated by that (in)famously massive rush of 'sea-salt',
...and ultimately, that will be the only reason anybody ever samples or even wears either scent.

But it is also still intriguing to attempt uncovering what other notes may be soaking in that brine:

Atlas seems fit to supply a more expected palette of accent notes that play along somewhat logically with a masculine mariner theme. These being namely, oakmoss, woods and aromatics, ...and by aromatics, I mean davana.

Megamare on the other hand, goes for a more whimsical 'niche' concept (perhaps typically atypical?) with
a musky, powdery, white floral accompaniment, which shifts the fragrance more into the unisex realm.

I really do like them both for what they are, though perhaps Megamare is more 'quasi-wearable',.
Truthfully, it is very unlikely I'll ever literally wear either out in public. ...though both are vital aromas to experience on a blotter.

miconi 10/12/25 22:37

I really wanted to like Megamare. I admire Orto Parisi for their bold, unconventional style, but this one just misses the mark for me. From the very first spray, it feels overly synthetic and chemical, with lab-made marine notes completely overpowering whatever natural materials might be hiding underneath.

Megamare doesn’t evoke the sea so much as a hyper-synthetic idea of it — metallic, plasticky, and sterile. Instead of waves, salt, and driftwood, I get more of a plastic white bag washed ashore, glistening in the sun. It’s conceptually intriguing, but emotionally and sensorially flat — something my nose simply can’t connect to on a natural level.

If the Bvlgari Aqva flankers capture the marine vision done right — that clean, salty, seaweed-laced freshness — then Megamare feels like their distorted mirror image, the sea viewed through cling film. I kept waiting for something organic to surface, but it never did.

Where it fails: the scent feels unbalanced. It desperately needs more natural citruses, more salt, a touch of seaweed, and the synthetics toned way down to let the composition breathe.

Verdict: clever in concept, harsh in execution. Definitely sample before buying — your nose (and wallet) will thank you later. And don’t you dare overspray, especially on clothes! You won’t wash it off easily.

2 sprays, forearm and chest, to test skin and fabric. At first blush, the obscenity of mangroves. Have you walked past mangroves at low tide? It's an experience that even someone who has lived on the beach their whole lives still struggles with.
An hour later, once the scent has had time to dry down and settle into the skin, briny seaweed on sunkissed skin with a touch of spice, an Australian Christmas. At this point, I had my coworkers ask me what they thought of it. First, they asked "what perfume?". Ah, so I wasn't imagining that the sillage became much more intimate in the dry-down. Perhaps it is that I have perfume-killer skin, perhaps it is that they were being polite to not notice it, perhaps it is just that my daily work scent Scandal Le Parfum is more aggressive still. After leaning in, most seemed to think it was "OK", "masculine", "very cologne-y", take it as you will.
After work, my skin smelled only slightly salty-musky-woody. My shirt retained the seaweed. Neither survived the wash. I have to assume many people are overspraying or are unfamiliar with the headache-inducing effects of ambroxan on many people to have given this perfume such a reputation.

Challenging at first, but charming and familiar once comfortable, so much like the sea itself.

Atrax Morgue 09/12/25 12:15

TLDR: Amazing year-round fragrance If you love musky marine scents with monstrous performance.

Megamare has earned a permanent spot in my modest collection for the foreseeable future. When I buy a perfume I try to think about specific situations where a particular fragrance will fit well in, and I try not to have too much overlap.

One situation that I always kind struggled picking a fragrance to wear in is rainy weather... until I discovered Megamare.
Coming from The Netherlands, it rains here often and during the cooler months it's also very overcast, which is the exact vibe I feel Megamare excels in.

Megamare is a pretty interesting marine scent. This is not a typical "fresh cologney" aquatic where it has some aquatic elements with a bunch of florals and fruits to make it pleasant. No, this is aquatic in it's truest form. It's kind of like being on the coast of the North Sea during low tide just before its about to start raining. You have the fresh sea breeze accompanied by some salty/musky wood covered in seaweed that's been sitting on the seabed for a while. This particular scent profile goes hand in hand with rainy or chilly overcast weather as I feel like it enhances that whole mood.

This fragrance is by design very synthetic, but that is also one of the reasons I love it (but some people don't). It has monstrous performance and if you spray it on clothes I guarantee you that that shirt will be smelling like Megamare even after multiple washes. I would say the scent itself is not the most pleasant in my collection, but under the right circumstances, it is an extremely enjoyable wear and as with other Orto Parisi fragrances, I get to enjoy it for hours on end too because I wont go nose-blind to it.

rylai 07/15/25 00:57

After a very long resistance, I finally got a sample to try. Orto Parisi fragrances tend to be very potent, and I expected this one to be the same; and it was.

The opening is a bergamot-infused marine scent. There's a sweet, almost watermelon-like note that appears, which is unfortunately common in many marine fragrances, though here it’s not overwhelmingly bothersome. There's also a rather intense salty note; possibly ambergris, given its saline character. A aquatic-mossy but tolerable green tone is present too, along with some woodiness.

In summary, the most prominent elements I sensed were salty ambergris, bergamot, and an algal nuance.
The sweetness gradually fades, and toward the end, a smoky and pungent note emerges. When tested on hair, this note becomes even stronger and more defined; whatever it is.

Overall, it's a nice marine fragrance. Strong and distinct.

Scent Of Dominion 07/13/25 05:16

My Take on Megamare by Orto Parisi

This one opens with a strong explosion of ambroxan, dense musk, and bergamot. The bergamot cuts through that iconic Orto Parisi musk, but instead of overtaking it, it stays layered on top along with hints of lemon, coexisting with the dominant ambroxan and musk. There’s also calone here, adding or imitating that distinct wetness you get from being submerged in water. For me, the seaweed note appears later maybe an hour into the dry down, depending on your skin chemistry. I don’t really detect the hedione, but perhaps it’s working in the background as a subtle support.

Megamare isn’t your typical aquatic or “fresh, clean” perfume. Maybe at the very beginning, but as it develops, it starts to drown you into the depths of the ocean. It creates an atmosphere that feels detached and isolated, yet confident, stoic, and undeniably powerful. If I had to compare it to any country, it would be Iceland beautiful, unique, but isolated and cold in its character.

For context, this is coming from someone who usually dislikes aquatic perfumes yet for some reason, I like Megamare. I don’t love it, but I do like it and respect it.

Oh, and the performance? Nuclear.

merlotsupernova 07/08/25 23:42

In Alessandro Gualtieri's olfactive mythology, where Risvelium embodies the Tarrasque, Orto Parisi's Megamare takes on the role of the Kraken... and if you don't know what I'm talking about, we don't need to be friends.

Megamare opens with a crisp blend of bergamot and lemon, giving way quickly to its dominant aquatic heart. Here, notes of seaweed, calone, and hedione create a robust marine accord. It’s a scent that will remind you of salty air, crashing waves, and the raw, untamed essence of the sea... if you want to romanticise those aspects.
The base settles into a long lasting combination of musk, ambroxan, and cedarwood, lending depth and a warmth that prevents it from becoming a boring fleeting fresh scent.

One of Megamare's most consistent attributes, frequently highlighted everywhere, is its remarkable longevity and projection. I tend to agree on the longevity side, whilst from a projection perspective I'd say that it is strong, but not nuclear.

Interestingly, while I’ve found that my wife didn't appreciate Atlas or Black Sea, she has a curious fondness for Megamare. Atlas, for her, possessed a green and almost "choking" tendency that she found unbearable (...and I agree). Its marine notes were perhaps too metallic or sharp. Black Sea, on the other hand, which hails from Pazzaglia and therefore has a slightly sweeter, softer overall profile with notes like orange blossom and ylang-ylang alongside its marine and salty accords, was still not to her liking, though less harsh than Atlas.

Megamare, despite its intensity and often challenging reputation, seems to strike a different chord, perhaps due to its particular balance of salty sweetness and deep musk, which avoids the green bitterness of Atlas or the specific sweetness of Black Sea that she found off-putting.
Of course we are talking about different price ranges, but this is another reason why you should sample when you can before buying a Kraken in a bottle - whichever declination you might decide to go for.

Megamare, respectfully, is a love-hate relationship in a bottle.

It’s incredibly powerful — and what seemed like a “safe” 3 sprays (one under the shirt, one on each shoulder) turned into a full-blown ocean invasion the moment I stepped indoors. If you're around people sensitive to strong scents, 1–2 sprays max. This is polarizing in every sense: people either love it or hate it — there’s no in-between.

It’s a true niche experience — salty, murky, aggressive, and dripping in musk. The opening is thick with seaweed, which I actually enjoy, though it leans just enough into a fishy vibe to throw some people off. Not rotten or offensive — more like uncooked. As it dries down, the saltiness becomes more dominant, and it shifts into something still marine but now almost metallic.

This isn’t your usual fresh aquatic. It’s dark, mysterious, and commanding. It's Poseidon rising from the ocean. Waves crashing into ships, sea creatures circling, dragging you into the depths. You don’t “wear” this fragrance — you survive it.

I’ve worn it to work and gotten compliments — one coworker even asked to hug me so the scent would rub off onto her clothes. But I’ve also had people react the exact opposite — making faces, whispering comments every time I walked past. I felt like a storm cloud in human form and the anxiety crept in fast. I’d start the day thinking “I smell amazing” and end up wondering “Am I too much?”

Still, I love it. It’s bold. It’s challenging. But whenever I do wear it I think, “I probably shouldn’t have worn this today.”

It’s extremely manly, raw and powerful, carrying the scent of saltwater spray mixed with wet, mineral, drenched stones. Pro_96 03/30/25 14:05

In the fragrance industry, the term “niche” is often associated with independent brands that specialize in fragrances. However, certain scents, such as “Megamare,” exemplify the true essence of niche fragrances. These fragrances are not universally appealing and may not resonate with most. Instead, they cater to a specific, ‘niche’ demographic.

On my birthday, a friend gifted me a clone of “Megamare” alongside the original. My intention was to thoroughly familiarize myself with the original before making an assessment of the quality of the clone. Consequently, I used this fragrance extensively.

Firstly, I must emphasize the exceptional projection of this fragrance. It is a room filler, and its longevity is remarkable, lasting over 10 hours on my skin after a single spray. However, it is advisable to limit the number of sprays to two, as excessive use can lead to anosmia and cause discomfort for both the wearer and those in close proximity. It is worth noting that this has the potential to cause nasty headaches.

In terms of scent profile, “Megamare” presents a unique and somewhat challenging scent to describe. It is difficult to pinpoint specific notes, but the overall, the scent is reminiscent of a blend of salty, musky, and seaweed scents, mixed with the aroma of the ocean on a warm day. One can envision a seasoned fisherman exuding this scent after a day at the ocean. While I neither find it particularly appealing nor detest it, the seaweed note in here possesses a distinct funkiness that I find quite unpleasant. Overall, the scent is linear and lacks significant evolution beyond this.

In terms of who can wear this fragrance - Individuals who enjoy the ambiance of the ocean, including the scent of wet rocks and sand, may find this fragrance suitable. It is appropriate for people of all ages, from teenagers to adults, but it is absolutely not blind buy safe and MUST be sampled. However, it is crucial to emphasize that this fragrance should not be worn indoors. Outdoor settings, such as picnics or beach days, would be ideal for enjoying its unique qualities.

This is the favourite child of the Orto Parisi family, and for a good reason. I got a sample of this, and had it sprayed all over my shopping bag when i went to pick up my bottle of Seminalis, and when I came home and left it in my living room, I got strong whiffs of it throughout the day, in the whole room. The opening citrus isn't what you'd expect of a citrusy smell, it's not in your face citrus, it's warmer, but still very fresh. Italian pigeon musk 08/21/21 11:14

Fragrantica should add a new meter on the longevity rating slider, right after eternal should be "megamare".

Longevity? Yes, this is another level. I sprayed this on a face cloth, 3 sprays and hung it in my bathroom last Friday (8 days ago, 180 hours ago), and when I walk in my bathroom I still get a whiff of it. Now mind you this is not putting my nose to the face cloth and still smelling a scent, this is 6ft from the door to the towel rack, (I measured it). I don't come closer than 2 feet to this face cloth and I get an occasional spritz of megamare. Which brings me to projection.

As far as projection goes, it acts exactly the same as the face cloth on my towel rack while you're wearing it. This does not radiate and fill up a room with a permanent inescapable scent that your constantly smelling everytime you inhale. It may be attached to the wearer or an object and filling an area with it's molecules, but you only get mild whiffs of it typically with movement. So it sits silently and reveals itself in the gusts of air passing your nose.

How does this smell? To me quite simply it's a mature slightly salty, musky, cold ocean air. There is warmth to the fragrance almost like the warmth of the ocean water acting like a blanket when you're submerged on a chilly day. But aromatically it's reminiscent of gusts of a salty cool ocean breeze.
The aquatic smell/note here is very raw, definitely synthetic, not very realistic to any real smells of the ocean but it's simplicity is very elegant and it does what it's intended to do "be marine". I definitely get a musk in this and probably ambergris or some synthetic version of it, both giving the marine note a mature fragrance vibe and adding perhaps a slightly salty sweaty vibe(not b.o.).

This wears like a perfume, it does not smell like you were near, around or in the ocean. It's not a scent projecting out an aquatic environment. It's a mature refined, relatively simple aquatic fragrance. It's classy. It has deep down a root that's present in all of the orto parisi fragrances, it's carries a particular vibe that you really need to smell to understand.

This is not a challenging scent, the only challenge to this fragrance is making a commitment to putting it on and figuring out how to get it off.

On skin this will survive a shower and sometimes multiple showers, on my skin it's actually hard to detect after about 8 hours, but it's still there. On clothes this is another story, I've managed to get it out of a tee shirt lightly sprayed after just one wash(laundry mat, commercial washers). Although I have had tee shirts that keep the scent through just one wash cycle.

I wore this to the gym on a sweatshirt and forget it, it still smelled pretty strong of megamare after one wash, so I just dedicated it to wearing this scent.

Fortunately I don't have much of a wardrobe it's mostly hoodies for the gym and plain white tee shirts and work clothes. If you have an extensive wardrobe and like to wear fragrances on clothes like I do, and you really like this scent, perhaps start planning on buying 2 pairs of everything, one for you and one for megamare.

I've worn this multiple times now, and this is really a scent that needs multiple wears to really appreciate. It's become quite an addictive captivating fragrance. I first tried it from a 1ml dabber and really was underwhelmed, It wasn't what I was expecting from the reviews I read, I thought it would be very loud and polarizing. Although I could tell there was depth to the fragrance and really needed to spray this thing and test it out a few times so I just went ahead and ordered the 50ml bottle. I would definitely order another bottle of this if or when it runs out. It's quite unique.

Back to the face cloth on my towel rack in my bathroom, still spritzing out wafts of this aroma, 8 days now. I'll try to update this review with the time in which this continues to not quit.

Edit:
Day 10 now, this hasn't let up on the face cloth. Still catching whiffs of it in and out my bathroom.

Day 11, four times now today caught whiffs walking into my bathroom. I think sometimes it's getting stronger.

Day 14, now 2 weeks on the face cloth, I caught a whiff earlier today taking a shower.

Day 16, I thought this was gone because I didn't recall smelling it in my bathroom yesterday, but today I got a big whiff of it walking in the bathroom and then again this afternoon.

Day 20 just when I thought it was gone, nope. Megamare creeping into the shower this morning.

Day 21 (3 weeks now), got whiffs of this walking OUT of my bathroom as it travelled in the steam created from the shower.

Day 25 ok so I think this has finally thrown in the towel(no pun intended), the past couple days I haven't gotten wafts of it in my bathroom, but I can smell it if I put my nose to the face cloth.
So I think it's safe to say you could classify megamare as a bargain fragrance. If you plan on wearing the same clothes for 25 days, you won't need to reapply. :)

aurora_ru 05/15/19 00:48

First impressions. Megamare starts out with sweet-dusty-crystalic-icy-blue-goo splashes, composed basically of big dose of Calone, Hedione, muscs and some popular synthetic ambergris material. I cannot say if it is Ambreton, Ambrarom or Ambermax, but something irritating, definitely not natural. If you are not afraid to dive into in, after seeing all this mega-polluted surface, then you can find something more clear and innocent under it, like sunrays breaking through the salty masses of ocean.

The heart of the fragrance does not sound aquatic to me at all, as it has fruity-ambery body, as lemon-apple punch, or pineapple, with some rhum, herbs and spices. In terms of aroma-materials it makes me think of something like Clearwood©. This heart of the scent is actually nice and reminds me very much of one fragrance I will describe later, but it is hard to stay there - the overdose of synthetic ambergris and sweetish aquatics is stifling me. Drydown is kind of woody-spicy, some drifted wood with some rhum and liquorice soaked in. And yes, it is impossible to air it out from the room and wash out of your clothes. Small annoying aroma-particles of Megamare will be stalking you everywhere like SmartDust.

The overall impression of Megamare is not AQUA or EAU FRAICHE, the structure of it is closer to commercial SPORT EXTREME FOR MEN fragrance (or as a parody of it?). Think Allure Sport Pour Homme Chanel meets Sauvage Sport Extreme Dior (Jack Sparrow edition).

I feel overwhelmed and depressed not so much by the fragrance itself, more by the situation. All that sauce of mystification and scandal over Gualtieri work and fancy. You know, the legendary Talented Mr.Gualtieri and his epic juices with unknown formulas, inspired by the dark side of life, lalala. And then there is Megamare itself as a creation, you try it and your nose knows immediately – it is just a agressive mix of contemporary materials.

I am not into this kind of scents, but 3 fragrances immediately come to my mind: Parfume.Sucks.Blue, Nebula Veil Oliver&Co and Archetipo Menditorrosa. I would compare this interesting heart of Megamare to Nebula Veil by Oliver&Co, I want you to notice the artistry and talent in one case and legitime negligeance in other. Veil is weird, avant-guard and experimental, yet beautifully composed and accentuated – we can actually feel and see the electromagnetic cosmic body of Nebula with distinguishable yellow (lemon) and violet (violets) veins. Meanwhile Megamare has similar sunny underwater element, but it is brutally coloured in blue, hedionised and calonised, using similar formula as in Perfume.Sucks.Blue. Lastly those stong ambergris elements reminds me a bit of that wet primordial stone in Archetipo. I don’t want to believe in plagiarism here, maybe this similarity is caused just by common aromamaterials. What makes me frustrated is this praised and marketed aura of Gualtieri. This king is so naked, yo guys, if we compare to some smaller brands.

0xrafae 01/07/24 01:09

Megamare is like tar in a black glass jar. If you spill it at home, you might pack your bags for a month, because the scent isn't going anywhere fast. It's a seriously intimidating fragrance.

Victor Mazz 01/22/25 16:17

Honestly ? I don't like it.

In my opinion it smell like a harbour, plenty of dirty water mixed with salt and the a dirty greasy metal of some ruined ship corroded by the salt. It's really musky, metallic, dirty, ozonic. Still not a refreshing scent so i wouldn't wear it in the summer. Projection and sillage are very good but you will get noseblind really quickly. Also the scent is super synthetic and it lacks natural that would give it a natural smell, i would have loved to be some more citruses.

Mark: 5.5/10, Underwelming, overrated.

If you want to try smething from gualtieri try seminalis. Gorgeous fragrance.
